items.title: Trump Administration Unveils Seafood Strategy to Boost U.S. Fishing Fleet and Domestic Production
items.original_title: Trump Administration Unveils Seafood Strategy to Boost U.S. Fishing Fleet and Domestic Production
items.summary: The Trump administration on Friday unveiled its America First Seafood Strategy, outlining plans to strengthen the U.S. commercial fishing industry through regulatory reform, investment in fishing vessels and shoreside infrastructure, and tougher enforcement against unfair foreign competition. The strategy , announced October 23, builds on President Donald Trump’s April 2025 executive order, Restoring American Seafood Competitiveness , and brings together several federal agencies to expand domestic seafood production, modernize processing capacity, and improve market access for American fishermen. The initiative comes as the administration pursues a broader effort to rebuild America’s maritime industrial base, including domestic shipbuilding capacity and the U.S.-flagged fleet. The administration also plans to strengthen the position of American seafood in domestic markets. Trade Representative will also work with other agencies to address unfair foreign trade practices and improve access to overseas markets for American seafood exporters. NOAA said progress will be measured through increases in domestic seafood production and processing, private capital investment, American jobs supported, and reduced dependence on foreign supply chains. The broader goal is to keep more of the economic value of American seafood in the United States, from vessels harvesting fish offshore to the shipyards, processors, and waterfront businesses that support the industry.

items.original_title: US waiver eases risks for India, China, but won’t alter Russian crude flows
items.summary: The US waiver on Russian crude has reduced uncertainty for Indian and Chinese refiners, giving them greater confidence to continue purchasing economically attractive Russian grades while keeping alternative supply options open in case the situation changes, analysts and industry sources said Oct. 22. The waiver is expected to preserve, rather than materially alter, Russian crude flows to India and China. “For refiners in India and China, the waiver is really about reducing the uncertainty rather than changing the crude supply picture,” said Premasish Das, executive director for oil analytics at S&P Global Energy CERA. “Past US decisions not to renew waivers reinforce caution: buyers may use the procurement window, but longer-term commitments will depend on greater confidence in policy continuity.” Russian flows to Asia intact Industry sources said India’s demand for Russian crude is expected to remain strong in the near term. Russian crude discharges in China — including pipeline imports — remained strong but volatile in 2026, according to General Administration of Customs data. Despite fluctuations, China’s Russian crude intake averaged about 2.35 million b/d over January-September, GAC data showed, underscoring sustained demand for discounted Russian barrels. Tariffs on China’s Russian oil purchases could reignite trade tensions with the US while doing little to deter such purchases, given the economic appeal of discounted Russian crude for Chinese refiners.

items.title: Sanctions risks reshape commodity trading
items.original_title: Sanctions risks reshape commodity trading
items.summary: In the briefing, authors Daniel Martin, HFW partner, and Amanda Rathbone, HFW knowledge counsel (commodities) said that sanctions compliance has evolved from a specialist legal consideration into a central strategic concern for commodity businesses trading oil, gas, metals and agricultural products. Martin and Rathbone warn that the sanctions environment is changing so rapidly that risks can evolve significantly during the lifecycle of a single transaction, from initial negotiations through to shipment, financing and payment. As a result, companies are increasingly being forced to reassess traditional compliance processes and adopt broader, more dynamic risk management strategies. Governments are increasingly using sanctions as instruments of broader geopolitical policy, meaning that ordinary commercial activity and seemingly routine commodity trades can now attract scrutiny. HFW warns that efforts to comply with one jurisdiction’s sanctions requirements can sometimes increase exposure to conflicting regulations elsewhere, creating difficult commercial and legal dilemmas for international trading businesses. The briefing also points to increasing expectations from regulators, who now expect companies to investigate broader sanctions risks throughout a transaction rather than relying solely on screening immediate contractual counterparties against sanctions lists. Martin and Rathbone believe sanctions complexity is unlikely to diminish.

items.title: Seafarers face widening competency gap as digital shipping accelerates, recent research finds
items.original_title: Seafarers face widening competency gap as digital shipping accelerates, recent research finds
items.summary: Eighty two per cent of maritime professionals surveyed say current training does not adequately prepare crews for the realities of modern, digitally-enabled vessel operations. Just 18% believe training keeps pace, according to new research from OneOcean and Thetius. Seafarer training is falling behind rapidly evolving operational realities at sea, according to two new reports commissioned by OneOcean and conducted by maritime innovation consultancy Thetius. Findings reveal two interconnected challenges – that seafarers work in increasingly complex digital environments, and that maritime professionals do not feel well prepared to keep pace with this change. Alex Mangan, Chief Marketing and Communications Officer, OneOcean, said: “Change in shipping will only accelerate as vessels adopt new digital systems to manage tightening international regulation and to sail more efficiently and productively. “This has created a growing gap between the training seafarers receive and the challenges they face at sea. Closing this reality gap requires the industry to shift its approaches to competence, to reflect real-world operations.” Nick Chubb, Founder of Thetius, said: “The findings reveal a clear reality gap between the demands of modern shipping and the way competence is developed. As vessels become more digitally complex, the industry must move beyond compliance-based training and equip seafarers with the skills they need to operate safely and effectively.” OneOcean’s own product suite reflects this thinking.

The proposal, outlined in a Federal Register notice scheduled for publication October 26, would extend the existing one-year suspension through January 9, 2027. Under the proposal, the measures would remain suspended from November 10, 2026, through January 9, 2027. The proposed extension also comes as the administration considers a much broader port fee system under its Maritime Action Plan , unveiled earlier this year. For now, the latest USTR proposal would leave the China-specific port fee measures on hold for another two months, while negotiations continue. USTR has opened a public comment period on the extension, with submissions due by 5 p.m. Comments can be filed through the USTR public comment portal under docket USTR-2026-0694. items.original_title: Record Tanker Rates Threaten to Push U.S. Oil Exports to Asia to Seven-Year Low
items.summary: By Yongchang Chin and Nathan Risser (Bloomberg) –US crude oil exports to Asia are set to hit multi-year lows after the Iran war disrupted global shipping and pushed the cost to lease a tanker for the Pacific journey to a record of almost $80 million. Asian refinery orders for US crude for delivery in November tumbled roughly 50% to 24 million to 26 million barrels this month sequentially, according to traders who asked for anonymity because they weren’t authorized to publicly comment. If that pace of orders holds through the end of this month, it would mark a seven-year low, based on ship-tracking data from Kpler and Vortexa. The tanker rate along the US Gulf Coast-to-China route has more than tripled since the US-Iran conflict erupted in late February to almost $60 million as of Thursday, according to Baltic Exchange figures. Those eye-watering rates doesn’t include the cost of the oil itself, which is trading around $100 a barrel. Tanker rates are so inflated that refiners are effectively spending $30 to $35 to haul each barrel of crude from the Gulf Coast to Asia, or as much as seven times what they shelled out last year, Hawkins said.

items.title: Singapore must look beyond the box to secure its logistics future
items.original_title: Singapore must look beyond the box to secure its logistics future
items.summary: Dropping behind Shanghai and Ningbo-Zhoushan in the global container port rankings, and seeing Malaysia’s Port Klang and Port of Tanjung Pelepas nip at its heels should serve as a wake-up call for Singapore, in a changing competitive landscape for box trades For Singapore, this is about more than losing a place in a league table. It is an existential question asking whether a nation built on maritime trade can adapt to a world where supply chain control matters as much as moving containers. As Singapore spent years living off its geographical advantages, deepwater harbour and reputation for efficiency to guarantee continued dominance, its competitors have expanded their infrastructure, attracted manufacturing investment, and developed integrated logistics ecosystems. Part of the problem for Singapore with its nearest rival is that it simply cannot compete with Malaysia when it comes to land availability, meaning it should not focus on warehouses and distribution centres. And the pending Tuas Port, with its planned capacity of 65m teu on full completion in the 2040s, will have a part to play, even if success cannot be judged by volume alone. Yes, the Ministry of Transport’s new Connectivity & Logistics division recognises the need to integrate maritime, aviation, and land transport, but creating a coordinating body will not automatically deliver the commercial agility needed to compete.

Tellingly, Hengli Heavy Industries announced today it had won orders for 52 ultra-large dual-fuel containerships: 20 of 24,000 teu; 20 ; of 19,000 teu; and a dozen of 22,000 teu. Maersk, which was dethroned from the top of the liner rankings in 2022 by MSC, is now eyeing a dozen 24,000 teu ships, up to 24 LNG dual-fuel 19,000 teu vessels and six at 18,600 teu. Zhonggu Logistics has entered the large ship segment, ordering a 14,000 teu pair at Hudong-Zhonghua for $155m each, joining fellow mid-sized shipping lines such as Emirates Shipping Line, Regional Container Lines, TS Linesm and China United Lines. Delivery is set for 2029 to 2030. items.title: NSR vs Suez: the Arctic is not a tradelane, it’s a corridor with a hefty premium
items.original_title: NSR vs Suez: the Arctic is not a tradelane, it’s a corridor with a hefty premium
items.summary: On 19 October, data from Norway’s Centre for High North Logistics (CHNL) showed 104 ships had crossed Russia’s Northern Sea Route (NSR) by 30 September, already more than in all of 2025. Four days earlier, Lloyd’s List Intelligence reported that containerships moved 2.19m teu through the Suez Canal last month, the most since the Houthi campaign began, and Linerlytica expects carriers to be fully back to Suez by the first quarter of 2027. Most coverage reads the first as proof that the Arctic is finally opening, but read together, they say something else: the part of the NSR Moscow planned and paid for has missed its targets by a wide margin, while the part it barely planned for has beaten them, because other people’s chokepoints closed. It isn’t that the NSR is missing from an Arctic section; the Arctic silk road itself is absent. Whatever the final figure, it is clear the season moved less than one 24,000 teu ship carries on a single Suez sailing. I costed the loop the way a carrier’s network team would: a 4,900 teu ship, eight seasonal sailings, west through the Arctic and back via Suez. The escort adds $150,000-$280,000 a transit, and Chinese sources put Arctic hull and P&I cover at three to five times normal rates.

items.title: South Korean Shipowner Sinokor Dominates Hormuz Transits as Oil Flows Rebound
items.original_title: South Korean Shipowner Sinokor Dominates Hormuz Transits as Oil Flows Rebound
items.summary: Oct 23, 2026 (Bloomberg) –A little-known South Korean shipowner dominated oil transits through the Strait of Hormuz in September, data from intelligence firms suggest, with the group’s vessels moving more barrels than the next three owners combined. Ships owned by Sinokor Group carried 105.6 million barrels of crude through the waterway connecting the Persian Gulf with global markets, an analysis of ship-tracking and other data from intelligence firms Vortexa, Equasis and Signal Group showed. That’s equivalent to almost 40% of oil making the crossing last month. of Saudi Arabia, also known as Bahri, the Kuwait Oil Tanker Company, and Abu Dhabi National Oil Co.’s shipping unit — accounted for a combined 97.3 million barrels during the same period, according to Bloomberg calculations based on that data. When Hormuz was all but closed off, those tankers were snapped up at exorbitant rates by producers who needed to load oil or risk running out of storage space and then being forced to undertake costly shutdowns. As Gulf crude exports recover to close to pre-war levels, Sinokor is still among the most active owners in the so-called shuttling trade, with its vessels taking short trips to pick up oil from inside the Persian Gulf, sail through Hormuz and then discharge at ship-to-ship transfer points in the Gulf of Oman.

items.summary: Russia was set to dispatch its first diesel tanker to the US on Oct. 22 after the Trump administration issued sweeping sanctions waivers aimed at reopening trade flows, according to Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak. It will be the first shipment of its kind to leave for the US since January 2022, before the US first sanctioned Russian energy flows. The deputy prime minister said earlier this week that Russia typically consumes 3.5 – 4 million metric tons/month diesel and exports 3.5 million mt/month, a figure he said the country can reach again by the year-end. Novak previously said that Russia is ready to supply 300,000 mt of diesel to the US in October, and a further 500,000 mt in November. Prior to the conflict, most of Russia’s diesel went to Europe, while shipments to the US were only nominal at 100,000 – 200,000 mt/month. items.title: MPA and Eastern Pacific Shipping Mark Christening of Singapore-Registered Ammonia Dual-Fuelled Vessel
items.original_title: MPA and Eastern Pacific Shipping Mark Christening of Singapore-Registered Ammonia Dual-Fuelled Vessel
items.summary: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and Eastern Pacific Shipping (EPS) marked the christening of Terra Clove at HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (HHI) in Ulsan, South Korea. The 93,000-cubic-metre Very Large Ammonia Carrier (VLAC) is EPS’ first ammonia dual-fuelled vessel and the first ammonia dual-fuelled commercial newbuild vessel to be registered under the Singapore Registry of Ships (SRS). It is equipped with Everllence’s first commercial ammonia dual-fuelled two-stroke marine engine, which successfully completed factory acceptance testing in April 2026. The vessel is the result of a collaboration initiated in June 2022 by MPA, EPS, HHI, and the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) to develop an ammonia dual-fuelled gas carrier under the Singapore flag. As Singapore’s flag administration, MPA has worked closely with EPS, HHI, ABS, and other industry partners on the vessel’s technical and regulatory compliance. This included reviewing the vessel’s design against relevant International Maritime Organization (IMO) guidelines, participating in hazard identification and operability studies, and providing regulatory guidance on ammonia detection, fuel system safety, and emissions management. MPA also shared its experience from earlier ammonia trials to support the development of onboard safety procedures and crew preparedness.

International Maritime Organization (IMO) Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez warned on Sunday that conditions had become increasingly dangerous, with reports of 24 ships attacked in roughly two weeks and no guarantees of safe passage through one of the world’s most important shipping routes. “The situation continues to be severe and critical when it comes to international shipping,” Dominguez told Fox News Digital, explaining that “there is a double blockade and too many vessels have been attacked, particularly in recent days.” The consequences for those working at sea have been particularly serious. According to the IMO, 100 maritime incidents had been confirmed across the region as of October 9, while 24 seafarers have lost their lives since the conflict began on February 28. “Seafarers have continued to perish in these attacks and around 6,000 seafarers remain trapped since the beginning of the conflict,” he said, making clear that his message was not to transit the waterway or put crews at further risk “until we have guarantees.” However, attacks on vessels are not the only concern.

items.title: India introduces new requirements for ships in coastal waters
items.original_title: India introduces new requirements for ships in coastal waters
items.summary: Expanded scope of the 2026 Rules India notified the Merchant Shipping (Regulation of Entry of Ships into Coastal Waters) Rules, 2026 on 16 September 2026. The Rules supersede the Merchant Shipping (Regulation of Entry of Ships into Ports, Anchorages and Offshore Facilities) Rules, 2012. The new regime applies to Indian ships and to foreign ships that operate in or navigate through Indian coastal waters, whether or not they enter an Indian port, anchorage or offshore facility. Under section 3(12): • “Coastal waters” means any part of territorial waters of India, along with any part of the adjoining maritime zones of India within the meaning of the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (80 of 1976), or any other law for time being in force; • It covers India’s territorial sea and adjoining maritime zones, including areas beyond the territorial sea where India has rights or jurisdiction under the relevant laws. Salvage and marine pollution response contracts Foreign ships entering, remaining in or sailing from an Indian port, seeking port facilities, or transiting or operating within Indian coastal waters are required to maintain valid salvage and marine pollution response contracts with an entity approved under the applicable Indian legislation.

items.summary: The Zero Emission Maritime Buyers Alliance (ZEMBA) has delivered 82,000 mtCO2-equivalent (mtCO2e) in emissions reductions in 2025 and 2026 under its first low-emission shipping tender with Hapag-Lloyd, which concluded this month. The reductions were achieved through the use of liquefied biomethane (LBM) across eight international shipping voyages under 17 contracts between Hapag-Lloyd and ZEMBA members. The German container liner secured ZEMBA’s inaugural tender to replace conventional bunker fuels with lower-emission alternatives. It then allocated environmental attribute certificates representing the emissions reductions achieved during these voyages to ZEMBA members through a book-and-claim mechanism. ZEMBA members include major cargo owners such as Amazon, Nike, IKEA and Patagonia. Second tender moves to e-fuels ZEMBA has awarded its second tender to Hapag-Lloyd and Norwegian shipping company North Sea Container Line (NCL), with fuel deliveries scheduled to begin in 2027. Hapag-Lloyd will use e-methanol on a trans-oceanic trade route, while NCL will deploy green ammonia on a northern European route. Both fuels will be produced using green hydrogen generated with renewable energy and are expected to deliver lifecycle emissions reductions of at least 90% compared with conventional marine fuels. ZEMBA expects the two companies to collectively deliver around 120,000 mtCO2e in emissions reductions over three years from 2027.

Each vessel will measure 26 m in length, with a load line length of less than 24 m, and will be built at Diverse Marine’s Cowes facility. All three newbuilds will share the same specification, be classed by Bureau Veritas and operate under the UK flag. The vessels are expected to support construction activities at an offshore wind project off the UK’s east coast in 2027, working alongside OEG’s existing Chartwell-designed Fulmar and Furioso . The order marks the second collaboration between OEG and Diverse Marine following the delivery of the Fulmar in 2025. That vessel has since supported construction work at Scotland’s Inch Cape offshore wind farm. items.summary: Mining giant Rio Tinto has approved a $1.9bn investment in a major bauxite expansion in Australia’s Queensland state, including an upgrade of its export facilities to accommodate larger capesize bulk carriers. The Kangwinan project on the western Cape York Peninsula will add 20m tonnes of annual bauxite production capacity, with first output targeted for 2029 and full production expected by 2032. The development will replace production from the ageing Andoom mine near Weipa, which is expected to reach the end of its life this decade, while also helping offset the planned closure of the Gove operation in the Northern Territory in 2029. Once fully operational, Kangwinan will lift annual capacity at Rio Tinto’s Weipa operations to around 44m tonnes, compared with current production of approximately 38m tonnes. The new mining centre will be located about 15 km southeast of Rio Tinto’s existing Amrun mine. A 15 km conveyor system will transport bauxite to expanded stockyards and the Amrun export wharf, which will be upgraded to handle larger capesize vessels. SEB further pointed out that shipments from Australia to China involve voyages roughly 3.3 times shorter than those from Guinea, where surging bauxite exports have been a major driver of capesize tonne-mile demand.

The increase initially started in the very large crude carrier segment and on Middle Eastern routes before spreading to all major crude trading routes, particularly affecting long-haul voyages. The bank identified five main drivers behind the $20 per barrel year-over-year surge in the average global crude freight rate. A war risk premium in Hormuz accounts for $7 per barrel, representing one-third of the increase in the global average crude freight rate. Inefficient tanker allocation and increased tanker redirections account for $3 per barrel, and the blockage of the Iranian fleet adds $2 per barrel by boosting demand for non-sanctioned crude tankers. Goldman Sachs expects these factors to continue supporting global freight rates as long as the conflict in the Middle East persists. The bank noted that high freight rates may reduce refiners’ overall demand for crude or shift it towards more closely located crude suppliers. On October 21, Brent crude was trading higher at around $110 a barrel on supply concerns, with traders wary of Red Sea shipping risks and threats to oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia from Iran-backed Houthi rebels. India imported 122.7 million tonnes of oil during April-September, largely unchanged from 121.8 million tonnes in the previous year. In September, the import bill jumped 46.6 percent to $15.4 billion, while volumes were up 6.8 percent at 21.7 million tonnes. The average price of Indian crude basket has risen to $121.25 a barrel in October from $65.08 from last year. The bigger risk for India is not the availability of crude but persistently higher landed prices that can inflate the import bill, widen the current account deficit and weigh on the broader economy, analysts say. The country imports around 1.8-2 billion barrels of crude annually and every $1-a-barrel increase in price raises the country’s import bill by up to $2 billion a year.

The results come as the canal continues to balance growing shipping demand with water conservation measures designed to protect operations during the developing El Niño weather pattern. Despite the challenges, the canal maintained a maximum authorized draft of 50 feet throughout the fiscal year’s dry season, providing relatively stable operating conditions for shipping customers. “Far from restricting trade flows, the Panama Canal facilitates international maritime trade by providing its customers with a reliable and safe route,” Panama Canal Administrator Ilya Espino de Marotta said during a conference call hosted by Bank of America Merrill Lynch. items.title: Follow the money or follow the flag? Politics clouds port investment
items.original_title: Follow the money or follow the flag? Politics clouds port investment
items.summary: In the seven years since TOC Americas last took place in Cartagena, global laden container volumes have slipped about 10% below where they would have been without the multiple disruptions that have hit the industry since 2018, according to Dinesh Sharma, director at Drewry Maritime Advisors. Sharma’s research measured growth from 2018 against forecasts of where the industry had imagined it would be today last time they met in Cartagena. Predicting the future, he said, was and is not easy. Transshipment hubs grew by about 6% a year on average over that period, against roughly 3% for gateway ports and 1.5% for the underlying economies they serve. The inefficiency, he said, is no longer contained at the big transshipment hubs: it is flowing through to gateways too, leaving Latin America’s overall throughput an estimated 2–3% below his 2018 projection. Washington’s growing interest in the region’s infrastructure raises the odds that port decisions get caught up in politics rather than commercial logic.

On the demand side, mills remain lossmaking and restocking is still on a just-in-need basis, with port inventories building again last week. Futures lost upward momentum after yesterday’s rebound and spot prices edged lower. Iron ore prices are likely to stay range-bound in the near term with limited upside, and import margins are expected to hold in modest positive territory. Source: SMM

items.title: European gas rallies on Persian gulf disruption pressure; Hot UK Inflation dents
items.original_title: European gas rallies on Persian gulf disruption pressure; Hot UK Inflation dents
items.summary: European wholesale natural gas prices surged on Wednesday, with both major regional benchmarks gaining over 3% as hotter-than-expected British inflation data and ongoing Persian Gulf energy disruptions heightened anxieties over winter fuel adequacy. The benchmark Dutch TTF front-month contract rose 3.1% to trade at 87.95 euros per megawatt-hour (MWh). In Great Britain, the equivalent NBP natural gas futures contract similarly advanced 3.2% to 216.57 pence per therm, with both contracts holding near their highest levels since late 2022. Wednesday’s gas rally coincided with fresh macroeconomic data highlighting the acute economic toll of elevated energy import costs on the British economy. Official figures showed Britain’s annual consumer price inflation accelerated to 3.5% in September, up from 3.1% in August and exceeding market consensus. Lacking large-scale long-term gas storage infrastructure, the UK relies heavily on real-time imports of pipeline gas and Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) cargoes to meet domestic power generation and home heating needs. The European benchmark remains up approximately 210% year-to-date. With maritime strikes and transit friction restricting LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz – keeping Middle Eastern deliveries to Europe nearly 80% below year-ago levels—European utilities face intense competition from Asian buyers for uncommitted Atlantic basin cargoes.

The extraordinary increase comes as Persian Gulf oil exports have actually surpassed prewar levels, highlighting the steep price of maintaining energy flows through one of the world’s most dangerous shipping corridors. According to The Wall Street Journal , citing vessel-tracking data from Kpler, Middle East oil shipments averaged more than 24 million barrels per day in the week ending October 18, exceeding the prewar average of 23.3 million barrels per day. In a separate analysis published Wednesday , the IEA said tanker rates reached historic highs in September and continued climbing into October, with the cost of transporting crude from the Middle East Gulf to Asia exceeding $37 per barrel by mid-month.

items.title: Nearly two-thirds of Far East-Europe capacity now back to Suez Canal
items.original_title: Nearly two-thirds of Far East-Europe capacity now back to Suez Canal
items.summary: Some 63% of the ocean capacity deployed between the Far East and Europe has returned to the Red Sea, following three years of detours, but some operators are hedging against renewed disruption by maintaining several Cape of Good Hope routes. Having surveyed the 10 largest carrier networks over the past month, Alphaliner found vessels on 24 of the 46 direct Far East–Europe services were transiting the Red Sea, accounting for 70% of deployed capacity on Far East-Mediterranean routes. On the Far East-North Europe trades, the number was a little lower, 58%, with containers moving between the Far East and Europe via Suez now topping 5.5m teu, of the possible 8.7m teu available to the trades – CMA CGM alone accounting for 1.3m of this. ABP confirmed the binding agreement in a London Stock Exchange announcement today. ABP operates 21 ports across Britain, including Southampton, Immingham and the Humber complex, handling around a quarter of the country’s seaborne trade. The deal brings an end to two decades of Canadian involvement in the port operator. OMERS was part of the consortium that took ABP private in 2006 for £2.8bn, while CPP Investments acquired its interest in 2015. IFM is owned by Australian and British pension funds and manages around $96bn in infrastructure assets globally. As Splash reported in August, the company is advancing a £500m development at Port Talbot in Wales to establish a major floating offshore wind manufacturing and assembly hub. Completion of the transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals and mandatory national security filings in the UK.

items.summary: Monaco-based shipowner Gestion Maritime is moving into the ultramax segment with an order for three 64,000 dwt bulk carriers at China’s Nantong Xiangyu Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering. The Danilo Fumarola-led company has booked the trio for delivery between late 2028 and early 2029, expanding beyond its traditional panamax and kamsarmax fleet. The vessels are costing in the low $30m range apiece, putting the overall investment at more than $90m. Gestion Maritime currently operates six panamax and kamsarmax bulkers and has recently trimmed its fleet through asset sales. The latest investment will bring smaller and more modern tonnage into a portfolio built largely around Japanese- and South Korean-built ships. The company, whose roots date back to 1908 and the Corrado shipping family, has traditionally pursued an asset trading strategy, buying ships when values ease and disposing of tonnage during stronger markets. In 2019, it exited the product tanker sector by selling two 2015-built MR tankers to Hafnia interests for $31m each, returning its focus to dry bulk. The newbuilding deal adds another international owner to Nantong Xiangyu’s growing customer base. The Chinese shipbuilder marked the delivery of its 100th ultramax bulker in July and has continued to attract orders for the 63,500 to 64,000 dwt segment.

items.title: Iraqi Line returns to Gulf container trade after 50 years
items.original_title: Iraqi Line returns to Gulf container trade after 50 years
items.summary: Iraq’s national shipping line is returning to scheduled container services in the Gulf after more than half a century, as the country seeks to rebuild maritime connections disrupted by the Strait of Hormuz crisis. According to Alphaliner, Iraqi Maritime Line is deploying the 902 teu Basrah on an eight-day shuttle linking Jebel Ali in Dubai with Umm Qasr, Iraq’s principal container gateway. The first sailing was scheduled to depart Jebel Ali yesterday, arriving in Umm Qasr two days later. Iraq’s transport ministry has described the initiative as the national carrier’s first regular Gulf operation since the mid-1960s. The relaunch comes as Iraqi container supply chains have been radically reshaped since the Hormuz shipping crisis erupted at the end of February. According to the Jordan Shipping Association, Aqaba handled 37,182 Iraq-bound transit containers during the first seven months of 2026, compared with just 3,599 during the corresponding period last year, a 933% increase. Hapag-Lloyd outlined a routing in July whereby containers are discharged at Khorfakkan, outside the Strait of Hormuz, before being trucked across the UAE to Sharjah or Jebel Ali and transferred onto third-party feeder vessels serving Iraq and other upper Gulf destinations.

items.title: Baltic Dry Index Rises Further to Near 1-Week High
items.original_title: Baltic Dry Index Rises Further to Near 1-Week High
items.summary: The Baltic Exchange’s dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, was up for a second session on Tuesday, rising about 1.9% to a near one-week high of 2,593 points. The capesize index, which typically transports 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, also advanced for a second day, climbing 4.7% to 3,522 points. Meanwhile, the supramax index was steady at 1,868 points; and the panamax index, which usually carries 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, fell by 1.7% to 2,247 points. Source: Trading Economics

items.title: Sedna and Nereus bring daily bunker prices for more than 450 ports into the conversations behind voyage decisions
items.original_title: Sedna and Nereus bring daily bunker prices for more than 450 ports into the conversations behind voyage decisions
items.summary: From HSFO and VLSFO to LNG and biofuel, chartering and operations teams can now check today’s bunker prices without leaving Sedna. Sedna, the Intelligent Operating System for Shipping, has partnered with Nereus, the intelligence platform for bunker and lubricants procurement, to bring bunker market prices into the conversations behind voyage decisions. The Nereus Bunker Indication Prices app, now live on the Sedna Certified App Marketplace, gives chartering, operations, and bunker procurement teams daily indication prices for more than 450 ports and six fuel grades, directly in Sedna Email. Until now, chartering and operations teams have had to get those prices separately, from a broker, a supplier or a market intelligence service, and bring them back into the email conversations where voyages are discussed and negotiated. Through the integration, Nereus updates its bunker indication prices every day and sends them to Sedna Email automatically.

items.title: Ports Are Scaling AI. Here’s How to Make It Deliver
items.original_title: Ports Are Scaling AI. Here’s How to Make It Deliver
items.summary: Ports and terminals are no strangers to reinvention. Over the past 50 years, the industry has managed and adapted to the shift to containerization and ever-larger vessels, the move from paper manifests to electronic messaging and transactions, and the subsequent evolution to system-to-system integration with other parties in the shipping industries. But many port functions still run on clipboards, radio calls, or the gut instincts of a planner, who has watched the yard fill up and empty thousands of times. To assess how far the industry has come, BCG and TIC4.0 (an international nonprofit association of terminal operators and equipment and solution providers dedicated to the creation and promotion of digital standards for the cargo-handling industry) surveyed more than 100 leaders from across the container ports and terminals ecosystem. On average, those we surveyed are already using or exploring the top 16 of the 43 use cases we assessed, from extracting data from shipping documents (62%) to predicting when a crane or straddle carrier will fail (48%). Survey Demographics In August 2026, BCG and the Terminal Industry Committee 4.0 (TIC4.0) surveyed the port and terminal ecosystem on the adoption of AI and generative AI, to establish where the industry sees the opportunity and where it sees the risk.
